name: 158. Passthrough reachability for surfaces without native routes (passthrough surface pins)
description: Rows for provider surfaces Bifrost has no native route for, covered through the catch-all passthrough routes, which accept arbitrary upstream paths for gemini (/genai_passthrough) and azure (/azure_passthrough). They prove the forwarding path for those surfaces is real, not that Bifrost models them: creating a Gemini tuning job or an Azure fine-tuning job is paid and is not exercised. Bedrock is not a catch-all passthrough: /bedrock_passthrough forwards only InvokeAgent, Retrieve and ApplyGuardrail, and folder 162 covers those operations. The /tunedModels body is carved out of the generic shape check in __skipShape.

item.name: 158.1 genai passthrough forwards a tunedModels list to Google (gemini tuned models)

exec: pm.test('Google answered the tunedModels list through passthrough', function () { pm.expect(j, pm.response.text().slice(0, 400)).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(j.error, 'Google rejected the list: ' + pm.response.text().slice(0, 400)).to.equal(undefined); if (j.tunedModels !== undefined) { pm.expect(j.tunedModels).to.be.an('array'); } });

item.name: 158.2 [EXPECT-4XX] genai passthrough forwards an operations lookup for an unknown name and Google answers not found (gemini operations)

exec: // Only Google's not-found answers this probe: a 401, 403 or 429 also comes back as a Google error
// envelope, but it says nothing about the unknown operation reaching Google.

pm.test('Google error envelope came back through passthrough', function () { pm.expect(j.error, 'not a Google error envelope: ' + pm.response.text().slice(0, 400)).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text().slice(0, 400)).to.eql(404); pm.expect(j.error.code, pm.response.text().slice(0, 400)).to.eql(404); pm.expect(j.error.status, pm.response.text().slice(0, 400)).to.eql('NOT_FOUND'); });

item.name: 158.3 azure passthrough forwards a fine_tuning jobs list to the Azure resource (azure fine tuning admin)

exec: pm.test('Azure answered the fine-tuning jobs list through passthrough', function () { pm.expect(j.data, pm.response.text().slice(0, 400)).to.be.an('array'); });
